structured.target: AC Biode CIIC 2024 circular waste syngas founders
structured.school_or_org: AC Biode (Japan- and Luxembourg-based clean technology company; founders met at University of Cambridge; CTO background Kyoto University)
structured.program_event: Climate Impact Innovations Challenge (CIIC) 2024 — East Ventures and Temasek Foundation; Grand Finale at Indonesia International Sustainability Forum (ISF) 2024, Jakarta Convention Center
structured.what_it_does: CIIC listing: scalable chemolysis of mixed organic waste to produce syngas for green energy generation. Company tech also includes Plastalyst (low-temperature ~200°C, water-based catalytic recycling of mixed/hard plastics into monomers) and AC Biodecomposer (hydrogen/syngas from organic waste); CIIC grant framed as piloting Plastalyst in Indonesia.
structured.place: Company: Luxembourg HQ with Japan (Kyoto) operations; also UK presence. CIIC pilot target: Indonesia (Jakarta finale).
structured.outcome_or_award: Winner, Circular Economy track, CIIC 2024. One of three winners sharing Rp10 billion (~US$645,894) grant funding to pilot solutions in Indonesia; AC Biode company post reports Rp3.3 billion grant for Plastalyst pilot in Indonesia.
structured.gap: No public source names a single student team or PH university for this entry—it is a Japan/Luxembourg startup, not an Ateneo/Youth CLAP project. CIIC winner quotes Habibur Rahman as Head Engineer of AC Biode, not as founder; founder roles are from ISC3/company profiles, not from the CIIC press kit. Exact split of the Rp10B pool is only stated as Rp3.3B for AC Biode on the company blog title/page, not independently itemized on the East Ventures/CIIC winners page. Whether the CIIC submission brand was officially "Plastalyst" vs "AC Biodecomposer" is slightly mixed across company pages (official CIIC text uses the chemolysis/syngas description only).
structured.note: SEA climate-tech reference (Indonesia pilot competition), not Philippine-founded. Useful for Youth CLAP circular-economy desk: waste→syngas chemolysis + plastic catalyst story; founded 2019 after Cambridge meeting; ~30 innovation awards claimed on ISC3 profile. Co-winners: SunGreenH2 (Energy Transition), Hydrogen Refinery (Sustainable Agriculture). Tracks for CIIC 2024 were Energy Transition, Sustainable Agriculture, Circular Economy.
